observations: A dark, roughly oval head shape dominates the center, built from dense black fill with scratchy white lines running across it like cracks or hair.
Two small rectangular eye shapes sit high on the face, each filled with crosshatch white lines, flanking a long vertical nose stroke.
At the bottom, five or six white tooth-like forms hang below the head's lower edge, tapering to points and separated by thin dark gaps.
reading: The face floats against a flat gray field, its mass almost entirely black, readable only through thin white scratches that map its surface. The eyes, small and gridded, sit high and close together, lending a look that reads as bewildered or mournful. Those dangling teeth—oversized, fang-like—shift the mood toward something more unsettling, a face caught between sadness and threat.
contextAngle: In the owned nifty faces subset, this work sits between #70 and #72. Where #70 explodes with saturated color and a wide grinning mouth, #71 strips nearly all color away. Its neighbor #72 shares the dark palette but introduces red marks and a skull-like structure.

connections.reason: Both use a dark background with a white-and-black face and prominent exposed teeth, but #72 adds red line work and a wider, flatter skull shape.
Both rely on heavy black fill with white contour lines to define a figure, though the nnotb work shows a full body rather than an isolated head.

lookingQuestion: How do the thin white scratches across the dark mass work differently on the hair-like outer area versus the interior of the face—do they describe surface, structure, or something else?
ambiguities: Whether the hanging white forms are teeth or tusks is unclear from the drawing alone.
The scribbled lines at the lower left and right edges may be a body or simply loose marks extending beyond the head.
